column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “my house” and “if it is good in your eyes”; BSB uses “my palace” and “if you prefer.”
The Hebrew explicitly says that Naboth spoke to Ahab; BSB leaves the recipient implicit.
The Hebrew says “his house” and “he did not eat bread”; BSB uses “his palace” and “refused to eat.”
The Hebrew names his spirit and bread in the question; BSB asks why he is sullen and refuses to eat.
The Hebrew leaves Ahab unnamed; BSB supplies his name.
The Hebrew explicitly says “bread” and “let your heart be good”; BSB uses “food” and “be cheerful.”
The Hebrew leaves the writer unnamed and repeats “letters”; BSB supplies Jezebel and uses a pronoun for the second occurrence.
The Hebrew says to seat Naboth “at the head of the people”; BSB renders this as a seat of honor among them.
The Hebrew calls the men “sons of worthlessness” and uses the verb “bless” in the accusation; BSB uses “scoundrels” and “cursed.” It separately says to stone him and that he will die.
The Hebrew explicitly names “the men of his city” and repeats the sending of the letters; BSB combines the men with the elders and nobles and condenses the instructions.
The Hebrew says to seat Naboth “at the head of the people”; BSB renders this as a seat of honor among them.
The Hebrew repeats the description of the worthless men and uses “blessed” in the accusation; BSB uses a pronoun for the repeated description and “cursed” for the accusation.
The Hebrew separately states Naboth’s stoning and his death; BSB combines them as being stoned to death.
The Hebrew repeats Jezebel’s name and separately states Naboth’s stoning and death; BSB uses “she” and combines the stoning with death.
The Hebrew repeats Ahab’s name; BSB uses “he” for the second occurrence.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats the downward direction when describing Ahab’s going to the vineyard; BSB leaves that second descent implicit.
The Hebrew asks whether he murdered and also took possession, without naming the victim or land; BSB supplies “a man” and “his land.”
The Hebrew begins with Ahab speaking to Elijah, without a separate arrival clause; BSB adds “When Elijah arrived.”

The Hebrew begins “Behold, I am bringing calamity,” without a new speech formula naming the LORD; BSB supplies that formula. It uses the images of urinating against a wall, being restrained, and being abandoned, where BSB uses “every male” and “both slave and free.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew makes the dogs and birds active subjects of eating; BSB makes the dead the subjects of passive clauses.
The Hebrew makes Jezebel the active subject who incited him; BSB expresses the inciting passively.
The Hebrew says he acted very abominably, without an explicit superlative; BSB uses “the most detestable acts.”
The Hebrew explicitly says he placed sackcloth on his flesh; BSB says he put on sackcloth.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “the calamity” in the final clause; BSB replaces it with “it.”
